evidence: paper: Z_j = (A_j, B_j, p_j, T_j), \qquad B_j = b_j(r,z,t)\,e_\theta, \qquad U_j = (\operatorname{curl} A_j + B_j,\ p_j,\ T_j)

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same three objects, repackaged. (i) Z_j: Lean's `representatives` indexes the tuple entries by `Entry κ = Bool ⊕ κ` — `.inl false ↦ A j`, `.inl true ↦ B j`, `.inr k ↦ R k j` — i.e. the paper's two scalar slots (p_j, T_j) are replaced by an arbitrary `[Fintype κ]`-indexed family of scalars; take κ a two-element type (or a singleton, which is the paper's own 'T_j may be omitted'). (ii) B_j: `angularField b w = (-x_2/r)·b(cylPoint w)·e_1 + (x_1/r)·b(cylPoint w)·e_2`, and e_θ = (-x_2/r, x_1/r, 0), so this is literally b(cylPoint w)·e_θ; `cylPoint w = (t, (r, z))` with r = radius w and z = w.2 2, so Lean's coefficient takes (t,r,z) where the paper writes b_j(r,z,t) — the same three arguments in another order. `exists_angular_realization` imposes exactly `B j = angularField (b j)` for j ≥ 1. (iii) U_j: `incrementComponents A B R j` is componentwise ((curl A_j + B_j)^i, R_k j), with `positiveStages` zeroing index j = 0, which is the paper's U_j for j ≥ 1. Lean also never needs U_j in isolation elsewhere: the partial sums U^{[J]} are built directly by `positiveStage`/`stageComponents` with the curl pulled outside the finite sum, which agrees by linearity of `spatialCurl`.
